title: Energy-Aware Deployment of Quantized Shallow-Water Image Enhancement on an Edge NPU for Underwater IoT Imaging

authors.name: Jiacheng Guo
affiliation: South China University of Technology, Guangzhou, China

abstract: Underwater image enhancement (UIE) research is trending toward heavy models, while lightweight alternatives are judged by parameters and FLOPs: proxies that say little about latency and energy on the edge accelerators underwater IoT platforms deploy. We report an on-device measurement study of shallow-water enhancement, whose per-channel attenuation physics favors compact quantized networks. Depthwise-separable U-Nets (9k-59k parameters) and a 4.3k-parameter curve model are trained on UIEB, quantized to FP16, INT8, and INT4 (palettized) with weight-only post-training quantization, and deployed via Core ML on the CPU, GPU, and Apple Neural Engine (ANE) of an Apple M3 Pro, with per-frame energy from idle-subtracted SoC power counters. The main 28.9k-parameter model at INT8 on the ANE enhances 256 × 256 frames at 945 FPS and 4.7 mJ/frame with no degradation at the reported two-decimal precision relative to FP16, and +3.2 dB PSNR over raw input on a 90-image held-out UIEB split. Across all 36 configurations on this FP16-compute stack, weight-only quantization provides no consistent latency or energy gain; energy is governed by compute-unit choice (3.6× vs. the GPU, 5.5-5.6× vs. the CPU) and network width. A W8A8 variant engages the ANE integer datapath (-18% latency, -28% energy at -0.37 dB), localizing the neutrality to weight-only PTQ rather than to the model or the NPU. A sub-30k-parameter network already saturates the measured quality-cost trade-off.
